cards.explanation: The answer is False. Jesus says, “For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.” The two are tied together. Whatever measuring cup you pick up for somebody else, I think you'd better like it.

The answer is beam. Jesus puts a speck in your brother's eye next to a beam in your own. A beam. In your EYE. I've done some silly things in my day, but nobody ever walked into my bakery wearing lumber on their face.

The answer is to take the beam out of your own eye. Jesus says, “First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.” Notice He says first. Clean up your own side, friends, then your view gets a whole lot clearer.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.” Beam out first, then clear sight. So He isn't telling anyone to stop helping. He's saying to get your own eye sorted out before you go digging in somebody else's.

The answer is that the pearls may be trampled underfoot. Jesus says that if you throw your pearls before swine, “…they may trample them under their feet…” He is talking about something valuable being treated as if it's worth nothing. That's a hard thing to watch.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “For everyone who asks receives…” Not some, not a few. The word is everyone, bakers, and He says the same about the one who seeks and the one who knocks.

The answer is Father. Jesus says, “…how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!” He starts with people who are evil but still know how to give good gifts to their children. Then He asks how much more the Father in heaven will give good things to those who ask Him.

The answer is the Law and the Prophets. Jesus says, “In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.” That's a lot of Scripture packed into one sentence, friends. I can't even fit a full batch on one tray.

The answer is destruction. Jesus says, “For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.” It's a hard line, so I'll say it plainly. Wide and easy is not the same as safe.
The answer is False. The first half is true, because the small gate leads to life. But Jesus says, “…and only a few find it.” So the statement fails on the word many. Few find it.

The answer is wolves. Jesus says false prophets come “…in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.” A cozy sheep coat on the outside and a hungry wolf underneath. That's quite the costume, friends.
The answer is bad fruit. Jesus says, “…every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.” The tree and the fruit match. It's the simple rule Jesus gives for recognizing people.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.” He doesn't leave a loophole, so a good tree doesn't sometimes bear bad fruit. The fruit shows what kind of tree it is.

The answer is that it is cut down and thrown into the fire. Jesus says, “Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.” It's a heavy line, and I won't dress it up. He is serious about trees that don't bear good fruit.

The answer is the one who does His Father's will. Jesus says, “Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.” Saying it isn't the whole thing, friends. Doing the Father's will is what He names.

The answer is “I never knew you,” and I think this one is heavy. Jesus says, “Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!’” He says it to people who listed what they did in His name. Take a quiet moment with that one.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!” The name for them and the command to depart are both right there in verse 23. Just before that, He says that not everyone who says “Lord, Lord” will enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 7:21).
The answer is on the rock. Jesus says the wise man “…built his house on the rock.” Everyone who hears His words and acts on them is like that man. The foundation is the whole story, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says the rain fell, the torrents raged and the winds blew and beat against that house, “yet it did not fall…” The storm is real, and the house still stands. I'd like to meet that foundation.
The answer is that its foundation was on the rock. Jesus says it did not fall “…because its foundation was on the rock.” It's not about how fancy the house looks. It's about what's underneath.

The answers are foolish and sand. Jesus says everyone who hears His words and does not act on them “…is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.” Hearing without acting is the problem, bakers, while the wise man hears and acts. Compare that sand with the rock the wise man chose, because the ground is what makes all the difference.

The answer is that it falls with a great collapse. Jesus says the house fell, and “…great was its collapse!” He says rain, torrents and winds beat against the wise man's house too, but its foundation was on the rock. This house was built on sand.

The answer is astonished. The Gospel of Matthew says the crowds “…were astonished at His teaching…” That's quite a reaction after a long sermon, friends. The next verse says why: He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.

The answer is True. The Gospel of Matthew says the crowds were astonished “…because He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.” That's the reason given for their astonishment. Jesus taught with authority.
